children.text: Electrons confined to a negligibly thin GaAs/AlGaAs layer have effective mass m*=0.067me. Ignore spin and random-potential scattering unless otherwise stated. A perpendicular field B points along +z and electric field is −Ey ŷ. The sample has length L, width W, area A=LW and N electrons. Take e>0 so electron charge is −e. A plateau occurs at RH=VH/I=3h/e². One vortex occupies a flux quantum h/e. For estimates use B=15 T, me=\(9.1\times10^{-31}\) kg, Coulomb constant \(9.0\times10^{9}\) SI, ε0=\(8.854\times10^{-12}\) F/m, εr=13, e=\(1.6\times10^{-19}\) C, h=\(6.626\times10^{-34}\) J s and kB=\(1.38\times10^{-23}\) J/K. In G a quantum point contact transmits independent carriers of positive charge magnitude e* at filling ν. The number nτ in time τ has Poisson law P(nτ=k)=λᵏe⁻λ/k!. Define noise as charge variance per time, rather than a spectral density with an extra factor of two.

statement.text:
Fractional quantum Hall effect
Electrons confined to a negligibly thin GaAs/AlGaAs layer have effective mass m*=0.067me. Ignore spin and random-potential scattering unless otherwise stated. A perpendicular field B points along +z and electric field is −Ey ŷ. The sample has length L, width W, area A=LW and N electrons. Take e>0 so electron charge is −e. A plateau occurs at RH=VH/I=3h/e². One vortex occupies a flux quantum h/e. For estimates use B=15 T, me=\(9.1\times10^{-31}\) kg, Coulomb constant \(9.0\times10^{9}\) SI, ε0=\(8.854\times10^{-12}\) F/m, εr=13, e=\(1.6\times10^{-19}\) C, h=\(6.626\times10^{-34}\) J s and kB=\(1.38\times10^{-23}\) J/K. In G a quantum point contact transmits independent carriers of positive charge magnitude e* at filling ν. The number nτ in time τ has Poisson law P(nτ=k)=λᵏe⁻λ/k!. Define noise as charge variance per time, rather than a spectral density with an extra factor of two.

a.i. Lorentz equation
Write the electron equation of motion.
a.ii. Stationary drift speed
Find the stationary speed vs.
a.iii. Drift direction
Which direction does the drift point?
b. Classical Hall resistance
Express RH using total flux φ=BA and N.
c. Filling fraction
Find ν=N/Nφ at RH=3h/e².
d. Coulomb energy scaling
Binding n>1 vortices to each electron increases their effective separation. Find α in the energy gain ΔU∝Bα at fixed filling.
e. One quasihole
At ν=1/3, find the increase ΔB that introduces exactly one positive quasihole of charge e/3 into area A.
f.i. Thermal scale
Calculate Eth at T=1.0 K.
f.ii. Confinement kinetic scale
Use uncertainty to estimate the kinetic energy of an electron localized in a vortex. Explain the length and momentum scales.
g.i. Mean tunnelling current
For the stated Poisson process find IB using λ,τ and carrier charge magnitude e*.
g.ii. Shot-noise variance
Find SI, the charge variance per time.
g.iii. Fractional-charge signal
Find SI/IB at ν=1/3.

children.text: \(m^*d\mathbf v/dt=-e(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)\). The effective mass belongs in the inertial term and the electron charge has negative sign.
Set the Lorentz force to zero. The transverse drift is \(\mathbf v_s=\mathbf E\times\mathbf B/B^2\), of magnitude \(v_s=E_y/B\).
Because (−ŷ)×ẑ=−x̂, electron drift is along −x. Conventional current is along +x.
\(I=Ne v_s/L=NeE_y/(BL)\) and VH=EyW. Hence \(R_H=BLW/(Ne)=\phi/(Ne)\), as a positive resistance magnitude.
There are Nφ=φ/(h/e) flux quanta, so RH=(h/e²)/ν. Thus ν=1/3.
The characteristic spacing is \(l_0\sim\sqrt{h/(\nu eB)}\propto B^{-1/2}\). Coulomb energy and its gain scale as e²/(4πε0εrl0), hence α=1/2.
One unbound vortex is one flux quantum. Thus AΔB=h/e, giving \(\Delta B=h/(eA)\). The flux increment does not become h/(3e).

A single-vortex length is \(l_0\sim\sqrt{h/(eB)}=1.66\times10^{-8}\,\mathrm m\). Taking Δp~h/l0 gives \(E_k\sim h eB/(2m^*)\simeq1.3\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm J\). Using ℏ instead changes numerical factors. This is an order-of-magnitude result, and the source accepts a factor 2π variation, so it requires self-review.
From ΣkP(k)=λ, the mean transmitted charge is e*λ. Therefore \(I_B=e^*\lambda/\tau\). The field uses q for e*.
The Poisson second moment is λ²+λ, so Var(nτ)=λ. Thus \(S_I=(e^*)^2\lambda/\tau\). The field uses q for e*.
The ratio is e*=νe=e/3≈\(5.33\times10^{-20}\) C. This follows the variance-per-time noise convention specified in the problem.

solution.text:
Fractional quantum Hall effect
a.i. Lorentz equation
\(m^*d\mathbf v/dt=-e(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)\). The effective mass belongs in the inertial term and the electron charge has negative sign.
a.ii. Stationary drift speed
Set the Lorentz force to zero. The transverse drift is \(\mathbf v_s=\mathbf E\times\mathbf B/B^2\), of magnitude \(v_s=E_y/B\).
a.iii. Drift direction
Because (−ŷ)×ẑ=−x̂, electron drift is along −x. Conventional current is along +x.
b. Classical Hall resistance
\(I=Ne v_s/L=NeE_y/(BL)\) and VH=EyW. Hence \(R_H=BLW/(Ne)=\phi/(Ne)\), as a positive resistance magnitude.
c. Filling fraction
There are Nφ=φ/(h/e) flux quanta, so RH=(h/e²)/ν. Thus ν=1/3.
d. Coulomb energy scaling
The characteristic spacing is \(l_0\sim\sqrt{h/(\nu eB)}\propto B^{-1/2}\). Coulomb energy and its gain scale as e²/(4πε0εrl0), hence α=1/2.
e. One quasihole
One unbound vortex is one flux quantum. Thus AΔB=h/e, giving \(\Delta B=h/(eA)\). The flux increment does not become h/(3e).
f.i. Thermal scale
\(E_{th}=k_BT=1.38\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm J\).
f.ii. Confinement kinetic scale
A single-vortex length is \(l_0\sim\sqrt{h/(eB)}=1.66\times10^{-8}\,\mathrm m\). Taking Δp~h/l0 gives \(E_k\sim h eB/(2m^*)\simeq1.3\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm J\). Using ℏ instead changes numerical factors. This is an order-of-magnitude result, and the source accepts a factor 2π variation, so it requires self-review.
g.i. Mean tunnelling current
From ΣkP(k)=λ, the mean transmitted charge is e*λ. Therefore \(I_B=e^*\lambda/\tau\). The field uses q for e*.
g.ii. Shot-noise variance
The Poisson second moment is λ²+λ, so Var(nτ)=λ. Thus \(S_I=(e^*)^2\lambda/\tau\). The field uses q for e*.
g.iii. Fractional-charge signal
The ratio is e*=νe=e/3≈\(5.33\times10^{-20}\) C. This follows the variance-per-time noise convention specified in the problem.
